ai.description: The Kakachi Shrub Frog is a small amphibian (20–25 mm) with a brown-mottled dorsum and distinct cream-white patches on the flanks. It features a pointed snout and granular skin texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Raorchestes kakachi* is best distinguished by its unique, vivid reddish-brown iris, which contrasts sharply with the more common golden or pale irises of similar species.
ai.habitat: The Kakachi Shrub Frog inhabits the mid-to-high elevation evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically found at altitudes between 1,000 and 1,300 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kakachi Shrub Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among foliage during the day and emerging at night to hunt for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes kakachi* undergoes direct development within terrestrial eggs, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon season, laying small clutches in vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Kakachi Shrub Frog is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu, India, specifically inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests above 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kakachi Shrub Frog produces a high-pitched, insect-like trill consisting of a rapid series of pulsed notes, typically heard from vegetation in mid-elevation forests.
